reviews.title: Es wird immer schlechter
reviews.text:
Ich nutze unter anderem Komoot, aber die App wird immer schlechter, seit der Übernahme durch Bending Spoons und kam nicht mehr empfohlen werden. 
Die App wird überfrachtet mit unsinnigen Funktionen (z.B. Gipfel zählen, Auf-/Abstiege zählen), die die App verlangsamen. Gerade im Gelände, weit ab von der Zivilisation gibt es meist nur sehr schwachen und schlechten Mobilfunk-Empfang. Je mehr Funktionen, desto mehr Datentransfer und desto längere Ladezeiten für das Programm, bis hin zu lädt überhaupt nicht.
Die letzte Änderung betrifft die Planung von Routen und macht alles unnötig kompliziert. Warum lässt man ein gut funktionierendes Tool nicht einfach so wie es ist oder baut richtige Verbesserungen ein, z.B. das Komoot Routenpunkte nicht eigenständig in der Reihenfolge verändert, obwohl das nicht gewollt ist.
Es Ärger mich auch, dass die Betreiber der App keine Rücksprache mit den Nutzern nehmen, denn meist sind es langjährige Nutzer, die auf Verschlechterungen hinweisen. Die neuen Nutzer kennen den Unterschied ja nicht.
Ein Austausch könnte zu Verbesserungen führen!

reviews.title: Katastrophe
reviews.text: Man kann die letzten Änderungen an der App nur mit dem Begriff „Katastrophe“ bezeichnen. Als Premium-Abonnent fühle ich mich maximal veralbert. Auf der Tour sind keine der bisher üblichen Informationen (Zeiten, Höhenprofil, Wetter, etc.) mehr verfügbar, da hat das Umplanen der Route keinen Sinn, wenn die Navigation nicht mehr funktioniert. Mit Ablauf meines Abo-Zeitraums werde ich kündigen und zu Outdooractive wechseln - mir reicht es mit diesen Software-Amateuren.

The app is useful for planning biking routes, but absolutely bonkers that free trial converts into a weekly subscription model. Just realized that I’ve been paying $5.50 USD a week on an app I haven’t opened in months.

I get it—we live in the world we do and I’m sure they disclosed the price I would pay after the free trial lapsed. But practically, no one expects to be charged WEEKLY (vs monthly) for this kind of app.

So just be mindful! If this review helps one person avoid losing $100, it will be worth it.

reviews.title: TikTok wannabe
reviews.text: This app is so useful for biking navigation that it is tragic that the entire experience is locked behind an idiotic UI designed to “engage” users over the utility it otherwise provides. I have no desire to use a navigation app as a social media tool and I deeply resent the developers’ insistence that I should. For example, you need to dig deep to uncover the actual navigation utility of the app. When you go to plan a route for the day you actually have to switch the command interface off it’s default setting, which is designed to let you “discover” routes nearby, rather than actually routing you to your destination; to do that, you have to press the “+ Plan” button. Ridiculous. Also, there is no clear way to end a route once you are finished with it. To do this you have to go into the “controls” button and then press a “Pause” button and then there are about 5 more pop up screens you have to click through to actually end the route. For a paid app, this is an absurd amount of effort to go through for basic functionality. I DO NOT WANT to use a navigation tool as a social media bit. I suggest the developers bifurcate the navigation tools from their attempt to be the TikTok of biking. Not every app needs to be a social media engagement platform. Stop this nonsense/ you are not TikTok and you never will be. Stay in your lane

Umso ärgerlicher ist es, wenn man sich auf eine Tour freut und dann trotz Komoot-Navigation plötzlich auf reinen Wanderwegen, Privatgelände oder Wegen landet, die einfach in einer Sackgasse enden.

Mein letztes Erlebnis am Gardasee hat dem Ganzen die Krone aufgesetzt: Auf einer einzigen Tour musste ich wegen der von Komoot vorgeschlagenen Navigation siebenmal umdrehen. Am Ende konnte ich die geplante Tour überhaupt nicht fahren.

Eine Navigations- und Tourenplanungs-App muss für mich vor allem eines können: mich zuverlässig auf einer tatsächlich befahrbaren Route ans Ziel bringen. Genau das funktioniert meiner Erfahrung nach bei Komoot inzwischen nicht zuverlässig genug.

reviews.title: Not impressed
reviews.text:
I downloaded this for a cross state long ride. The app would not reroute when going around closures and would just constantly tell me that I was off route. Once I got further away from civilization it was routing me away from towns that had services (such as being able to get water). At 110 miles the lock screen widget froze up leaving me to have to unlock my phone and look at the app for the next 67 miles. It also routed me onto a busy 65 mph divided highway for 2 miles. I’m pretty sure it was legal but not somewhere most people want to bike. 

I also tried a route that was in the app already. It was mostly okay except trying to take me down a gravel road that was poorly maintained and when I used Google Maps to get me around it, that wouldn’t give me directions until I got back to the main road because even Google knew it wasn’t a road to bike on. 

On the plus side I loved the lock screen widget while it worked.

reviews.title: Easily the most annoying app
reviews.text:
I have bought and been using the app for the last 2 years more or less. 
Prons: when you use it for famous, well documented paths and strictly do as the app says, then it’s kind of ok. 
Cons: 
1. The constant “restore purchase” message. I have to manually restore my purchase every single time and the app is asking to buy it again. Very annoying 
2. Do not dare to change direction or alter anything on a hike. It will keep telling you to go the other way or not be able to caption things properly. It has a single cell for mind and that’s what you should follow. Otherwise it just keep screaming to change direction etc. 
3. The paths that it suggest multiple times don’t exist or are much harder than described. Exposed paths, non existent paths and many other things have happened to me with hikes I found in the app. 
4. The review system is designed not to allow you actually review a path but only review it for the algorithms sake. Multiple times I wanted to let other hikers know of the path conditions, difficulty and dangers and never had the chance. 

Overall it’s a really bad, deeply frustrating app with lots of misleading information. I hate it and regret buying it.

reviews.title: Your route is being adjusted, make a U Turn
reviews.text:
It’s hard to believe the developers have tested and approved this application. I tested it today and have the following critique.
1. As The route planning doesn’t differentiate between footpaths and bridleways you can plan a route only to find some of it isn’t permitted by bike. Why wouldn’t you correct this or give a bike permissible route feature?
2. When navigating it doesn’t give consistent way finding cues.
3. If you need to adapt your route on the fly the systems keeps chirping - Adjusting your route….make a U Turn! It keeps repeating this message which indicates that it clearly isn’t adjusting the route as a normal sat nav would do. 
4. If you’re riding on the road parallel to the cycle path it gets confused and says Turn left, then turn right, then turn left, then turn right.
5. Sometimes the cues are too early or too late. There is no affirmation of a correct turn or an incorrect turn.

Overall the route planning is inadequate if you’re doing off road routes. The inability of the app to re-route you via the nearest permissible route makes it total impractical as you have to stop and keep checking where you are against the planned route. Definitely not worth the subscription fee. Avoid.

reviews.title: Blatant greed

The fact that Komoot requires a subscription to push routes to a Garmin device is absolutely abhorrent. I have no interest in paying $5 monthly or $60 annually for that feature. I’m perfectly willing to pay a reasonable one-time fee of $30, but locking basic functionality like route syncing behind a subscription is nothing short of blatant greed.
I’m exhausted by the endless subscription model, and even more so by companies that strip away features and then charge recurring fees to get them back. Until Komoot stops this predatory approach, I genuinely hope the app continues its decline. Newer users getting serious about backcountry navigation would be wise to stay away and simply use other apps or manually export/import GPX files instead.

reviews.title: Don’t spend your money
reviews.text:
I needed a simple route planner for my custom rides. I don’t want to share the routes with anyone else. It’s a pain to go into settings to make everything private. Privacy should be the default since I’d rather my address (starting point) NOT be shared with everyone. 

When making rides that start and end at the same point, this app has a stroke if the custom waypoints cross previous sections of the route. If I’m selecting, let’s say, waypoint 9 of my ride, and I try to cross an earlier section in the path, it’ll keep resetting the waypoint to 1 and mess up the entire route. It’s a pain to have to go into the trip settings and drag what was supposed to be waypoint 9 from the #1 spot to the #9 spot where it’s supposed to be. 

I like there’s an option to set waypoints to go off grid, but once again, the app is very finicky when setting these waypoints, and it’ll often mess up the numbering sequence. 

I’d be willing to pay money for the premium plan, but your app can’t even set simple waypoints in order from start to finish without messing up. I don’t want it to automatically try to shorten the route. I want to go where I tell it to. Such a simple thing. I will be looking at other apps.

reviews.title: Offline mode is a joke
reviews.text:
Unlike All Trail and Google Maps, Komoot's offline maps require network to power their app before you can even access the trail maps you've downloaded, which defeats the purpose of OFFLINE and posed serious safety risk for my trip in the Lake District, where network is a scarce resource. Luckily I realised the problem before setting off and spent two hours manually syncing the GPX files to my Garmin watch (network was very choppy at campsite). Should've just gone old school rather than blindly trusting technology since my Garmin never failed me and uses satellite connections instead of signal towers.

Advice to Komoot's product and engineering team: you know how downloaded Netflix content would work even in flight mode? Your users will need that too because we aren't able to open your app on a hill when signal is weak and therefore impossible to rely on the maps we downloaded.

The app is focused on social networking features, not route planning. The social features are the landing page and the routes you are working on are buried in your profile. when you find the routes you are working on, the editing functions on the iPhone app are buggy and poorly organized for task. Numerous small glitches, like hamburger menus (three bar icons that indicate a menu) that don’t do anything next to the waypoint list (if you can find it, it’ll take a few minutes).

Many little features show lack of consideration for users. If you tap feedback, thinking this will give you a chance to lodge a bug report, it only opens up an gas page — clearly indicating they are not interested in receiving bug reports, which would help both them and the user.

Maybe this is better on Android — I don’t remember it being so bad there. Or maybe it is this latest version. But I’d avoid the iPhone app for route planning. reviews.title: Not easy to plan route
reviews.text:
I started the premium subscription a few days ago because I’ve heard great things about Komoot. However, I’m disappointed with its unintuitive interface so far.

I tried planning a route and wanted to return to the same path I had sent. Unfortunately, it tried to redirect me to a different route. I had to manually adjust the points to match my desired path.

It would be great if Komoot could incorporate natural language commands for route planning. I haven’t noticed this feature yet.

I also attempted to plan a long-distance walk, but the estimated completion time was discouraging. It seemed to assume that I was slow based on my activity level. I believe this is because Komoot doesn’t have access to my personal fitness data.

It would be beneficial if Komoot could allow me to input my fitness level, such as my biking, walking, and running speeds. This way, it could provide a more accurate estimate tailored to my abilities rather than relying on a generic baseline.

I understand that Komoot may not have access to my personal fitness data since I’m new to the app and haven’t used it for walks yet. However, I hope that Komoot will eventually incorporate this feature.

I’m glad I’m still trying out Komoot and haven’t made any financial commitments yet.

reviews.title: Misleading upsell screen
reviews.text:
I’ve paid for the World Maps pack and only use this app occasionally for hiking, so I was surprised and disappointed to find that every time I open the app I’m presented with a full-screen Premium subscription prompt.

The screen strongly implies that payment is required to continue, with pricing options and a large “Continue” button prominently displayed. The only way to proceed without subscribing is a very small “X” in the corner. While technically optional, this design feels intentionally misleading and unnecessarily aggressive.

As a paying customer, I shouldn’t have to dismiss a subscription upsell every single time I launch the app. It creates the impression that the features I’ve already paid for are somehow restricted unless I subscribe again.

I understand companies need to promote premium services, but this approach feels like sharp practice rather than transparent communication. A simple, occasional reminder would be far more acceptable than a persistent, full-screen paywall-style prompt.

I’d gladly continue using and recommending the app if this heavy-handed upselling were reconsidered.
